cards.text: Friend, Joshua 12 is a roll call of the kings the Israelites struck down and whose lands they took. I spent years in a junk drawer counting dust, so believe me, I was BORN for a list. We start east of the Jordan, from the Arnon Valley all the way up to Mount Hermon.

Two kings held that side: Sihon king of the Amorites, and Og king of Bashan, "one of the remnant of the Rephaim." Now THAT is a title, friend, and the only title I ever had was a price sticker that said 25 cents! Moses, the servant of the LORD, and the Israelites had already struck them both down.

cards.question: Moses and the Israelites took the land of Sihon and Og. So what does Moses do with all that land?

answers.text: He gives it to some of the tribes as an inheritance
He holds it for himself as Israel's leader
He sets it aside until the war is over

cards.question: Moses handled the two kings east of the Jordan. Now the action moves WEST. Who leads the Israelites against the kings over there?
Joshua is the one leading Israel now, and he conquered the kings west of the Jordan. True or false: Joshua keeps that land under his own rule.

cards.text: Out west, the land runs from Baal-gad in the Valley of Lebanon to Mount Halak, hill country, foothills, wilderness and the Negev, the lands of the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites. Then comes the roll call, and every king gets the same little tag: the king of Jericho, one, the king of Ai, one, then Jerusalem, Hebron, Lachish, Hazor, one, one, ONE, all the way down to the king of Tirzah. Add it up and it's thirty-one kings in all, and friend, I counted dust for YEARS and never once got a total that good.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 2 quotes "one of the remnant of the Rephaim.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the introduction of Sihon and Og, the price-sticker joke, and the statement about Moses and the Israelites striking them down.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Cards 3 and 4 are both discovery questions: the earlier cards do not say how Moses allocated the eastern land or identify Joshua as the leader of the western conquest. Two of the stop's three choice cards therefore require luck rather than reasoning, leaving at most one informed guess.

rule.text: A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
